title: Charging a Missed Scheduled Payment on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan
content:
# Charging a Missed Scheduled Payment on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

**Finance desk desk-book entry.** Where a scheduled payment on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan is not made in time, the finance desk books a charge for that lateness against the plan's billing history for the one missed payment due date it answers. The charge goes on as a new positive entry carrying the lateness code given and dated and cycled on today's date, and the customer sees it on the next statement; the plan record's own balance and delinquency fields are not touched.

## Invoking `book_lateness_charge_0092ea40`

The agent unlocks `book_lateness_charge_0092ea40` and calls it. One call books a single charge for one missed due date.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | What it is | Format or values |
|---|---|---|
| `financing_plan_id` | The reference number of the promotional financing plan record the charge is booked to | An identifier, read from the financing plan lookup for this customer before the call |
| `lateness_charge` | The money charged for the lateness | In USD as a positive number with 2 decimal places, half-up at the cent, with no currency symbol and no thousands separator; an empty value is not accepted |
| `payment_due_date` | The payment due date that was missed | Written as YYYY-MM-DD in the store's own calendar dating, exactly as it is printed on the statement for that billing cycle and read from the plan's billing history |
| `fee_code` | Which priced charge this entry is | One of the values below |

**The values `fee_code` takes.** Use `late_fee_first` when the entry is the opening lateness charge of the run being priced; `late_fee_repeat` when an earlier lateness already counts against the plan in the stretch being read; `returned_payment` only where the entry prices a payment the bank sent back; `deferred_interest` only where the entry bills held-back promotional interest; `paper_statement` only where the entry prices a posted paper statement; `prepayment` only where the entry prices clearing a plan ahead of its term; and `not_applicable` only where the entry prices nothing at all.

**Return.** A single confirmation sentence in plain text naming the reference number minted for the new billing entry, the plan reference it was booked to, the missed due date it answers, and the charge as booked in USD to two decimal places. That sentence naming the new entry reference is what indicates the charge is on the billing history.

## Points of judgement

- The call books the figure it is given; the figure itself is worked out from the plan's records and this desk's published rules before the call.
- The entry is dated and cycled on today's date, while the due date it answers is the one the parameter carries.
